name: Living in agreement with Nature
plain_explanation: For the Stoics, the whole universe is a single, unified, rational and divine system called Nature; a good human life is one whose will is deliberately aligned with this rational order, rather than one that merely happens, passively, to be part of it (as everything, even a criminal's actions, technically is).
precise_definition: The Stoic ethical ideal that the individual will should actively conform to Nature/Reason/God (three names for the same governing cosmic principle), as distinguished from the trivial sense in which every event, virtuous or not, is already 'in harmony with Nature' simply by being caused according to natural law.
why_it_mattered: It is the positive formulation of Stoic virtue, and the source of the famous image (Cleanthes) of the wicked man as a dog tied to a cart -- compelled to follow Destiny either way, but only the virtuous man follows willingly rather than being dragged.
historical_origin: Central Stoic doctrine from the school's founding.
associated_philosopher: Cleanthes (for the 'dog tied to a cart' image); developed throughout the school's history
examples: Cleanthes's prayer: 'Lead me, O Zeus, and thou, O Destiny... I follow fearless, or, if in mistrust I lag and will not, follow still I must'
influence_on_later_thinkers: Marcus Aurelius's Meditations restate this ideal repeatedly ('Everything harmonizes with me which is harmonious to thee, O Universe').
connection_to_politics_or_religion: Identifies God, Nature, Destiny, and Reason as a single governing principle -- a form of pantheism.
